- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >80) — cap forecast at +10% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; adjust downward by 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture early sentiment-driven corrections — apply a 1–2 day lag correction: if sentiment drops on day N, reduce forecast for day N+1 by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model is prone to averaging bias — use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5-day history to anchor forecast.
